user.title: Choose a transmitter
user.description: Which radio should talk to the fireplace, and on which band. 315 MHz is the North American variant; 433.92 MHz is the European one.

receiver.title: Choose a receiver
receiver.description: Which radio hears the fireplace handset. Setup needs one: the next step learns the handset from a single button press. Afterwards it keeps Home Assistant in step with the handset. Preselected is the radio behind the transmitter, if it can receive; any other listed radio works too.

retry.title: Nothing was heard
retry.description: No frame arrived in a minute. Check that the receiver is listening on the right band and is within range of the handset, then try again.

reconfigure.title: Change the radios
reconfigure.description: Which transmitter reaches the fireplace, on which band, and which receiver hears the handset. The handset already learned is kept. Leave the receiver empty for a transmit-only setup: Home Assistant still controls the fireplace but no longer follows the handset.

abort.no_transmitters: No radio frequency transmitters are set up. Add one first, such as HackRF Proxy.
abort.no_compatible_transmitters: No transmitter can reach 315 or 433.92 MHz with OOK.
abort.no_receivers: No radio that can receive is set up, and setup learns the handset by listening. Add one first, such as HackRF Proxy or an ESPHome device with a radio frequency receiver.
abort.transmitter_unusable: That transmitter is no longer in the entity registry.
abort.receiver_unusable: That receiver is no longer set up.
abort.already_configured: This handset is already set up.
abort.reconfigure_successful: The fireplace now uses the new radios.

progress.listening: Listening. Press any button on the fireplace handset now — this only reads what the handset transmits and changes nothing about the appliance.

init.title: Fireplace settings
init.description:
Pick a temperature sensor and this fireplace gains a thermostat that regulates the flame from it. Leave it empty for no thermostat.

The thermostat only decides how hot; it does not decide whether the fire should be lit at all. Conditions like nobody being home belong in an automation, which is where they can see the rest of the house.

The fireplace cannot be asked what state it is in, so Home Assistant re-sends the state it believes whenever the radio has been quiet for the interval below. That is what corrects a command the appliance missed, or a handset press heard by nobody. Set it to 0 to never re-send.

data_description.reconcile_interval: Minutes of radio silence before the believed state is transmitted again.
